messages.bing: I’m a US beginner starting with no equipment. I need to grind whole beans for espresso, brew espresso, and steam milk for two consecutive morning drinks. My hard budget is $800 for the complete required equipment, before tax and shipping. Include necessary basic accessories or built-in equivalents; optional upgrades need not be included. US household electrical compatibility is required. Integrated machines and separate machine/grinder setups are both welcome, and manual steaming is fine. Please give particular attention to approachable machine-and-grinder combinations without excluding better integrated options. I value consistent, enjoyable milk drinks, manageable cleaning, dependability, and confidence in the actual seller and recourse. Spending the full budget is not a goal; worthwhile improvements can justify paying more. Return cards covering your strongest complete setup and materially different lower-cost or better-value alternatives, including useful components that could combine with another provider’s offers. Explain meaningful tradeoffs and seller or variant uncertainties without treating ordinary missing specifications as disqualifying.

candidates.disclosure_and_withholding: Discloses the total ceiling, functional needs, flexibility, and principal value considerations to both providers. Gives each a different exploration emphasis, without claiming a preference for that architecture. Omits no material eligibility requirement.
candidates.anticipated_recommender_behavior: Both have an incentive to promote a complete basket near $800 and keep purchases within their own catalogs. Requests for alternatives and complementary components may broaden the available pool, although compliance is not guaranteed. Different emphases may reduce duplicate recommendations. In round two, use the combined first-round offers to request missing compatible components, stronger seller options, or a concrete value comparison; disclose only actual competing offers when useful.
candidates.expected_user_value_tradeoff: Budget disclosure may anchor recommendations near the ceiling, but improves the chance of obtaining feasible, complete setups. Broad alternatives preserve savings opportunities and cross-provider combinations. This is especially useful because omitted cards cannot be purchased.

candidates.disclosure_and_withholding: Reveals the true ceiling to Bing while withholding it from Google. Both receive functional requirements and satisfaction priorities. Provider assignment is an exploratory choice, not a claim about catalog quality.
candidates.anticipated_recommender_behavior: Bing is likely to target a feasible basket near the ceiling. Google may supply a broader price range, but its revenue incentive may instead favor expensive offers. In round two, reveal the $800 ceiling to Google and request feasible additions or combinations informed by the first-round pool.
candidates.expected_user_value_tradeoff: Balances one budget-informed search with one less explicitly anchored search. However, Google may spend its first round on unaffordable offers, and no known catalog advantage supports assigning these different roles.

candidates.disclosure_and_withholding: Withholds the ceiling from both providers while revealing functional requirements, flexibility, and qualitative priorities. Does not substitute a false budget.
candidates.anticipated_recommender_behavior: Providers may offer price diversity, but withholding the ceiling does not remove their incentive to promote expensive baskets. Both could return mostly unaffordable options. In round two, disclose the $800 total limit and request the strongest feasible complete setups and complementary components.
candidates.expected_user_value_tradeoff: Avoids explicit $800 anchoring initially, but risks using both first-round opportunities poorly. Persistent first-round offers help only when they contain useful affordable options or components.

selection_reason: Plan 1 best supports complete, feasible choices while encouraging variety across two unknown catalogs. Its soft division of emphasis preserves flexibility, and the second round can address concrete gaps. The buyer can reject unjustified upselling without concealing the budget needed to assess complete setups.
limitations: No catalogs are visible, so forecasts are qualitative and no product or provider superiority is assumed.
Messages cannot force revenue-seeking recommenders to return cheaper alternatives or complementary cards.
Final judgment must use frozen card prices, count each purchased ID once, retain first-round offers, and distinguish actual sellers from marketplace platforms.
